memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord God said, "It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him." — Gen 2:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Up to this point in the creation story, a certain phrase has echoed again and again: "God saw that it was good." Light was good, the seas were good, the living creatures were good. So it stops us in our tracks when God now says something is not good. And what is it? "It is not good for the man to be alone." We were not made to live in isolation.

This tells us something God built into us from the start. We are made for relationship—first with Him, and also with one another. God, who Himself exists eternally in loving fellowship, created us to need companionship too. The word translated "helper" is a strong and honouring word; Scripture even uses it of God Himself as our helper (Ps 121:2). It speaks not of someone lesser, but of a needed partner.

While this verse leads directly to the gift of marriage, its truth reaches wider. Many walk through seasons of loneliness—the single, the widowed, the far-from-home. Hear this gently: God sees your aloneness, and He calls it "not good." He cares about it.

The deepest answer to our loneliness is found in Christ. In Him we are drawn into God's own family and joined to His people, the church, where no believer need walk alone (Heb 10:24–25). And He promises never to leave us (Heb 13:5).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you allow yourself to need others, or do you try to manage life alone?
- How might God be inviting you into deeper fellowship with His people?
- Where do you need to remember Christ's promise never to leave you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that You made me for relationship and that You see my lonely moments. Draw me closer to You and to Your people, and remind me that in Christ I am never truly alone. Amen.
